standard_prerequisites.name: The standing situation (axioms A, B, C)
standard_prerequisites.statement: A dg category with the distinguished-triangle axioms, in particular the admissible short exact sequence attached to a morphism and its associated triangle (the author's Situation situation-ABC, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the two admissible sequences, their structure maps and the associated triangles (source lines 3784-3798, 3800-3810).

standard_prerequisites.name: Cone of a morphism and its structure maps
standard_prerequisites.statement: The cone c(f) of a morphism with the maps realising it as the middle term of the admissible sequence, and the identities among those maps and their differentials.
standard_prerequisites.use: The component c is built out of those maps and verified using the identities (source lines 3805-3827).

standard_prerequisites.name: Commuting up to homotopy
standard_prerequisites.statement: The given square commutes up to homotopy, that is, the two composites differ by the differential of a homotopy.
standard_prerequisites.use: The homotopy is one of the ingredients of the matrix defining c and is what makes the computation work (source lines 3786-3791, 3811-3826).

core_obligations: Recall the two admissible sequences and their structure maps given by axiom (C), and state the identities among the structure maps and their differentials that the standing situation provides (source lines 3800-3810).
Define the third component: build c : c(f_1) -> c(f_2) as a matrix whose entries are the given maps a, b and the homotopy between the two composites (source lines 3811-3820).

Verify the compatibility: compute the differential of c, use the displayed identities (for instance d(pi_1) = f_1 b_1 and d(s_2) = a_2 f_2) to show that c is a degree-zero morphism of the dg category and is compatible with the maps y_i -> c(f_i) -> x_i[1], so that it is a morphism of triangles (source lines 3820-3829).

proof_roadmap.step: Collect the two admissible sequences, their structure maps and the identities among them.
Define c as the matrix built from a, b and the homotopy.
Verify that c commutes with the differentials and is compatible with the structure maps.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-cone at source lines 3778-3798: in the standing situation, a square of morphisms of complexes that commutes up to homotopy gives rise to a morphism of the triangles associated to the two morphisms, which is one of the axioms making the homotopy category triangulated. The proof at source lines 3800-3830 is an explicit construction of the third component c and a verification that it is a morphism of degree zero compatible with the structure maps. The construction uses the admissible short exact sequences supplied for each of the two morphisms, writes c as a matrix built from the given maps and the homotopy between them, and then computes its differential, using the identities among the structure maps and their differentials (displayed in the proof) to show that c commutes with the differentials and is compatible with the maps to the shifted objects. Each identity used is a separate computation and the statement records none of them. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
